text:
maya: quick brainstorm — we need a fresh latency vs cost narrative for the Q2 webinar + one launch post. can we map 3 customer archetypes to 3 visuals and one hero chart? :thinking_face:
jordan: love that. which archetypes are we thinking? startups (PLG), mid-market (SaaS product teams), and enterprise (SLA + private deployment)?
kevin: yup. for visuals: 1) scatter: latency (ms) on x vs $/1k tokens on y, color by deployment mode. 2) waterfall: how batching + KV cache reduces cost per token. 3) SLA tradeoff bar: unit cost vs guaranteed p99 latency buckets.
sophia: + a tiny callout venn diagram for where Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private is the sweet spot. keeps product placement obvious without heavy text. :white_check_mark:
noah: for the hero chart, what if we do a 2-axis combined: left axis = median latency, right axis = $/1k tokens as a dotted line. show three curves for small/medium/large prompt workloads. simple and tangible for non-engineers.
maya: sounds good. need 2 narrative hooks: "same model, different serving economics" and "how serving choices change unit economics and SLA risk". not too academic — emphasize practical decisions (when to cache, when to quantize, when to move to Dedicated).
jordan: copy ideas: short hero line for social — "Lower latency, lower surprises: pick the serving strategy that fits your product". subtitle: "We benchmarked real workloads and mapped the tradeoffs between latency and cost."
kevin: data asks for visuals: can eng-ml export CSV with: model, deployment_mode, median_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens, batch_size, cache_hit_rate. bench-bot: generated on demand.
bench-bot: hey! I can export recent benchmark slices to /internal/bench/2026-02-econflow.csv on request. use `bench-bot export --slice econflow --format csv`
sophia: timeline? workshop with design + eng-ml tomorrow? we need first drafts for the webinar slides by EOD Thurs.
maya: ok assign: kevin — coordinate with eng-ml for CSV + sample queries; jordan — draft hero copy and social variants; sophia — lead visuals with design; noah — inbound routing notes + demo plan. i'll own the webinar outline and post draft.
kevin: pinged eng-ml in DMs, they said new slice available in ~6 hours. will post CSV link here when ready.
jordan: social variants: 1) short tweet: "Latency or cost? You shouldn’t have to choose. Here’s how serving strategy makes the difference -> link" 2) LinkedIn long form with chart explainer 3) blog hero post with reproducible bench notebook.
sophia: design constraints: keep axes readable at social size, avoid log scales unless we annotate. prefer scatter with jitter and small table inset for key numbers. will sketch by tomorrow noon.
noah: inbound flow: add two CTAs on landing — "Get cost estimate" (small self-serve calculator, capture company size + model usage) and "Request Dedicated trial" (enterprise form). route leads: small -> marketing-nurture, mid-market -> AE SDR, enterprise -> solutions-eng.
maya: good. also add an eval prompt set link for the "quality vs quantization" note — we need a one-slide appendix showing quality delta at 4-bit. kevin can append eval metrics.
kevin: will include BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics + qualitative sample outputs in the CSV export note.
jordan: we should A/B the hero line: variant A uses cost-first framing, variant B uses latency-first — run small paid social test for CTR.
sophia: also add animation for streaming vs batched token delivery in the webinar demo. simple side-by-side user-perceived latency.
maya: next checkpoints: kevin posts CSV + sample table here (by +6h), sophia wireframes by tomorrow noon, jordan first-draft copy by EOD today, noah inbound routing doc + form fields by tomorrow. i'll compile into the deck Thurs morning.
kevin: CSV link: https://internal.storage/bench/2026-02-econflow.csv — includes fields requested. sample row: "gpt-like-v2,hosted,85,210,0.0045,8,0.32"
jordan: nice. can someone make a 30s explainer gif for social from that scatter? design + eng could export frames from viz.
sophia: can do. will mock in Figma and export GIF frames for approval.
noah: inbound form fields draft: company_name, company_size, region, expected_monthly_tokens, primary_use_case, estimated_latency_requirement, contact_email. will push to /ops/forms and share the URL.
maya: thank you team. final ask: keep language audience-friendly — product managers should immediately see the decision levers. follow-up thread after design review. :rocket:
